pcs.pc_description: ensure that visual inspections of the body components for cracks are performed
regularly clean the dust in the air filter bowl
examine the bucket cutting edge and the lift for signs of excessive wear
examine the moldboard, tilt cylinders, pipes, and hoses for leaks or damage
make certain that the loader's structure and arms are not damaged
check for any damage or leaking in the transmission, fuel tank, axles, and hydraulic tanks
check sure the oil levels in the engine, hydraulic tank, fuel tank, gearbox, radiant coolant, and braking are within the manufacturer's specifications
periodically recharge batteries
drain moisture from air tanks in case it is equipped with air brakes
carry out inspections to ensure that the parking brake, main horn, reverse horn, and headlights are in good working order
get a visual inspection to check the different controls, gauges, warning lights, and other safety devices
wear seatbelt and adjust the seat position
clean the dust bowls of the air filters and inspect the gasket and inner filter
drain the water and debris from the fuel tank
ensure that all greasing pins and pivots points are appropriately greased
before starting the wheel loader, go all the way around it to make sure no one is beneath or on it
ensure that all safety and maintenance stickers are visible on the equipment
maintain a inspection/maintenance logbook in which all operations completed prior to starting the wheel loader are recorded
notify the supervisor immediately if a defect is discovered that is outside the scope of the position

pcs.pc_description: plan and organize the job according to given instructions
examine the jobsite for loose soil, concealed deep ditches, or marshy spots where the backhoe might become trapped
perform all pre-use and on-the-job inspections
wear a seatbelt and adjust the seat position
start the engine using the pushbutton switch and key switch
use the priming pump and pre-heater to start the engine when it's cold outside
calculate the machine's speed and direction based on the function given
in the event of a crisis, press the emergency stop button to turn off all power to the wheel loader, according to the operator's handbook
to load, unload, transport, or stack items, move levers or controls that drive lifting equipment such as forklifts, lift beams with swivelhooks, hoists, or elevating platforms
inspect product load for accuracy and confirm with the supervisor
examine the product load for accuracy and check with the supervisor
material should be placed beneath, over, or around loaded pallets, skids, or boxes, in accordance with the work description and safety precautions
secure items for transfer to specified places in accordance with supervisory instructions
safely move load around the facility to ensure timely and complete delivery
move controls to drive equipment that transports goods between loading, processing, and storage locations
when necessary, alert personnel to discharge, dump, or level items
hook tow trucks to trailer hitches and fasten attachments, such as graders, plows, rollers, or winch cables to tractors, using hitch pins as per SOP
turn valves and open chutes to dump, spray, or release materials from dump cars or storage bins into hoppers
estimate the appropriate amount of load to be loaded on the wheel loader to prevent over loading the machine during operations
after completing operations, switch off the ignition
after use, ensure that the gear is in the neutral position
after using the equipment, leave it idle for a few minutes
remove attachments after use
removed attachments should be cleaned and stored in a safe place
ensure that the machine is shut down and secured when left unattended
in the event of an equipment failure, run the machine in limp back mode according to the instructions in the operators handbook
follow reporting procedures as laid down by the employer
in a timely way, complete all documents in accordance with the required requirements
